tasks.short: Collaborate with professionals and providers on patient care

steps.what: Review patient care context and identify issues for collaboration
Collaborate with health care professionals and agree care responsibilities

tasks.design: Retain the specialist's review and direct collaboration with the care team. The {OTHER} clinical record remains the source of patient context; changing its presentation does not remove clinical review or agreement time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Care coordination involves competing assessments and real service constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared clinical records can provide context, without deciding responsibilities.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving disagreement and ensuring a provider can carry out the agreed action.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise conflicting care needs and negotiate a workable plan.
tasks.altitude: Care coordination rights and meeting time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a clear interdisciplinary care handover

evidence.claim: Clinical collaboration requires contextual review and agreement between responsible professionals.

assumptions: Boundary covers specialist preparation and participation, not other professionals' encounter time or subsequent treatment.

The treating professionals produce dated findings and care plans in routine care outside this boundary, unchanged. The specialist reconciles their relevance and produces the agenda in s1; missing entries require direct clarification within retained time.
No structured action list is assumed to exist before the discussion; responsibilities emerge in s2.
Review native shared-record and handover views before custom development; none is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because there is no changed tool or capture obligation. Any time shared with another conference task must be allocated once.
unknowns: Access across providers and actual preparation burden
research_questions: Which recurring coordination failure is caused by unavailable information rather than unresolved clinical judgement?

already_counted.description: Preparation and collaboration remain fully counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Both routine coordination and conflicting assessments keep their preparation and discussion time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read literature and participate in professional learning

steps.what: Find current nursing literature and screen candidate sources
Read current literature and appraise relevance to nursing practice
Discuss developments with colleagues and participate in professional conferences

tasks.design: Configure saved searches and source alerts in the {OTHER} literature database before building anything. The specialist still screens results, reads full material in {DOCS} and participates in professional discussion; no generated summary replaces reading.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated searches consume time, but relevance cannot be established by keywords alone.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved searches and metadata filters can reduce repeated retrieval.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing study quality and deciding whether findings transfer to the specialty.
tasks.human_edge: Connect evidence limitations to real nursing practice and challenge colleagues' interpretations.

ambition.what: Revisit one defined specialty learning question when a relevant new source appears

tasks.altitude: Less repeated searching; no new authority to change care standards.

reach.learn: Search strategy, appraisal and separating learning from protocol approval

evidence.claim: Saved literature searches can reduce repeated retrieval while leaving critical appraisal and discussion intact.

assumptions: Boundary includes finding, reading and discussing professional material; protocol development is separate and not an added saving here.

Database publishers produce title, author, publication date, source identifier and abstract as existing publication metadata, with unchanged producer effort. The specialist selects search terms, checks metadata and relevance in the retained half of s1; new periodic filter review costs two hours per 100 baseline hours.
Missing metadata, incomplete coverage or inaccessible full text returns to manual search in s1; alerts never determine clinical applicability.
Use native database alerts and subscription access first. No custom integration, automatic source appraisal or patient data processing is assumed.
The 20/50/30 split is an E1 scenario to validate, not an observed baseline.
unknowns: Available saved-search functions, licence access and proportion of repeated search effort
research_questions: Do native alerts halve retrieval time without missing important sources in a sampled learning question?

already_counted.description: Screening candidate sources and correcting searches remain.
Full reading, appraisal and professional participation remain.

incremental.description: Review source coverage and adjust saved searches.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=90, gross=10 less two upkeep hours gives net=8. High assumes repeated searching is halved; low assumes only two hours are released because coverage gaps require manual search. Reading and conferences are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop, implement and evaluate specialty nursing standards

steps.what: Appraise evidence and define requirements for nursing standards
Draft specialty nursing standards from appraised requirements

loop.purpose: Express appraised requirements in a consistent standard structure
loop.input: Specialist-selected evidence passages, requirements, exclusions and existing standard
loop.output: Draft clauses linked to source passages and an unresolved-questions list
loop.check: Specialist checks every clause for changed clinical meaning, conditions, exclusions, unsupported recommendations and omitted requirements against full sources
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported or unresolved clauses return to manual drafting
loop.why_not_simpler: Native document structures handle formatting first; translating heterogeneous prose into clauses still requires language judgement

steps.what: Verify final nursing standards and submit for governance approval
Implement approved nursing standards and evaluate practice outcomes

tasks.design: Use the native standard structure in {DOCS} first, then a bounded drafting loop only for wording from specialist-appraised evidence. The specialist verifies meaning, governance approves the exact final version, and implementation and evaluation retain their full effort.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rewriting appraised material takes time, while clinical recommendations need accountable judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded language tool can prepare source-linked draft clauses for full review.
tasks.still_hard: Determining evidential strength, local feasibility and whether a standard improves care.
tasks.human_edge: Own the clinical interpretation and evaluate actual practice after implementation.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft composition; evidence appraisal, implementation and approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Outcome selection, practice observation and change governance

evidence.claim: Source-constrained language drafting is plausible, but savings and clinical fidelity need local testing.

assumptions: Boundary includes evidence appraisal through implementation evaluation; no saving is claimed for gathering evidence in another task.

The specialist produces source identifiers, exact passages, population, conditions, exclusions and proposed requirement in s1. This capture and appraisal remain fully counted; incomplete packets use manual drafting, with no automatic clinical inference.
Native document templates and version control are tested first; a model is used only for semantic wording.
Governance review remains ten original share hours, outside the focal denominator, with no transferred labour saving. Roll-up must reconcile any shared policy-development effort.
No patient-identifiable material is needed for drafting. Actual professional and governance authority must be verified locally.
unknowns: Drafting share, governance route and permitted drafting environment
research_questions: Does blinded clause review find omissions or altered recommendations after drafting assistance?
Is composition time reduced after counting full verification?

already_counted.description: Appraisal, final verification and implementation evaluation remain.
Draft review and manual exceptions remain.

incremental.description: Specialist audits drafting fidelity after source or model updates.
Document owner maintains structures and validates access and tool updates.

approvals.approved_version: Final verified text, source packet and unresolved-issue disposition; any change requires renewed specialist verification
Exact specialist-verified standards version, effective scope and implementation conditions; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Focal B=90 and R=80: gross=11.11 less two focal upkeep hours gives net=9.11. High assumes drafting time halves; low assumes only upkeep-equivalent time is released because clauses require extensive rewriting. Appraisal, governance and implementation remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain departmental procedures and infection control standards in practice

steps.what: Locate current departmental policies, procedures and infection control standards
Interpret departmental standards and identify deviations or unclear requirements
Maintain adherence to procedures and address infection control deviations

tasks.design: Configure the controlled policy view in {DOCS} to show current effective versions and relevant department filters. The specialist still confirms applicability, interprets requirements and maintains adherence in practice; automatic search does not decide infection control actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the current approved policy can take repeated navigation through old documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document metadata and controlled views can reduce that lookup.
tasks.still_hard: Applying a general standard to an unusual clinical situation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise deviations, coach staff and escalate an ambiguous requirement.
tasks.altitude: Less policy navigation; responsibility for adherence stays the same.

reach.task: Help review a local procedure's usability
reach.learn: Version control and distinguishing interpretation from policy amendment

evidence.claim: Controlled document views can reduce version lookup without automating clinical interpretation.

assumptions: Interpret maintain as following and sustaining current departmental standards, consistent with the supplied work activity. Developing new standards belongs to the separate development task and is not counted again.

The existing document owner produces policy identifier, department, version, approval status, effective date and superseded-version link during controlled release. Existing release effort remains outside and unchanged; two additional other-role hours per 100 focal baseline hours allow metadata correction for the configured view.

The specialist verifies version and applicability in retained s1 time. Missing or contradictory metadata sends the user to the document owner and manual library search; it never treats an unknown version as current.
Test native library filtering first; no custom clinical answer generation or new patient monitoring is proposed.
Fifteen percent retrieval is an E1 scenario; savings fall if native navigation already works well.
unknowns: Current metadata quality and time actually spent finding effective policies
research_questions: Does the configured view locate the correct effective policy faster in realistic specialty cases?

already_counted.description: Version and applicability checks remain in lookup.
Interpretation and maintaining practice adherence remain.

incremental.description: Specialist checks view relevance and reports missed or obsolete entries.
Document owner corrects metadata and tests controlled views.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=92.5, gross=7.5 less two focal upkeep hours gives net=5.5. High assumes lookup halves; low assumes small retrieval gains only offset upkeep. Interpretation and adherence work are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The specialist spends less time on repeated source retrieval and first-draft wording while retaining evidence appraisal, care coordination and practice oversight.
reach: Lead a focused evidence discussion with registered nurses
Coordinate a limited standards implementation evaluation
role.ambitious_version: A specialist who notices relevant evidence sooner and prepares clearer standards for existing governance, without automatic care decisions.
